item.text:
The 2022 record is narrow on Tshisekedi’s own private honesty, but it does contain a real personal-nexus thread: a close adviser’s corruption scandal, the presidency’s response, and a separate ruler-ordered anti-corruption audit of public assets. I did not score the chapter.

**Reused Evidence**
- `REUSE_JSON: {"evidence_ids":["E0001"],"lenses":["7B.1"]}`

**New Evidence**
- OCCRP is the strongest direct item on the governing circle. It documents Vidiye Tshimanga, described as one of Tshisekedi’s closest advisers, offering mining licenses and protection in exchange for a stake, while describing proxy and offshore concealment.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"I Will Take My Percentage: Congolese Presidential Adviser Caught on Tape Negotiating Corrupt Mineral Deal","publisher":"OCCRP","publication_date":"2022-09-15","url":"https://www.occrp.org/en/investigation/i-will-take-my-percentage-congolese-presidential-adviser-caught-on-tape-negotiating-corrupt-mineral-deal","claim":"Vidiye Tshimanga, described as one of Tshisekedi's closest advisers, was recorded offering mining licenses and protection from bribe-seeking officials in exchange for a stake, and he described hiding the share through proxies and offshore trusts.","locator":"lines 57-64, 68-74, 117-123","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Investigative reporting with named reporters, direct recording excerpts, and follow-up confirmation from the subject, though the tape-makers were unidentified.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly within 2022 and centered on a senior member of Tshisekedi's governing circle.","ruler_attribution":"Indirect but material: the conduct is by a presidential adviser who repeatedly invoked his proximity to Tshisekedi; this is not proof Tshisekedi personally took money.","contrary_evidence":["Tshimanga denied wrongdoing and said he was being set up; OCCRP could not identify who made the recordings."],"lenses":["7B.3","7B.4","7B.5","7B.9","7B.10"]}
- Reuters adds the presidential-office response: Tshisekedi’s communications director said corruption was one of the president’s pillars and that anyone in the Office of the President who violated the law would suffer consequences.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Top Congo presidential adviser resigns after allegedly requesting bribe on tape","publisher":"Reuters","publication_date":"2022-09-16","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/top-congo-presidential-adviser-resigns-after-allegedly-requesting-bribe-on-tape-2894087","claim":"Reuters reported that Tshimanga resigned after the tape and that Tshisekedi's communications director said the fight against corruption was a pillar of the president's action and that anyone in the Office of the President who violated the law would face consequences.","locator":"lines 429-431","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters is a high-quality wire source; it reports the resignation and reproduces the presidential-office statement, though the underlying allegation comes from a separate investigation.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Within 2022 and tied to the Tshisekedi presidency's immediate response to a corruption scandal in his circle.","ruler_attribution":"Direct to the presidential office response, but not a personal quote from Tshisekedi himself.","contrary_evidence":["The adviser denied wrongdoing and the statement did not mention Tshisekedi personally."],"lenses":["7B.6","7B.7","7B.10"]}
- Radio Okapi shows the judicial follow-through: the prosecutor opened an inquiry and asked the anti-corruption agency to investigate the alleged 20 percent commission and influence-peddling allegation.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"RDC : ouverture d'une information judiciaire à l'encontre de Vidiye Tshimanga","publisher":"Radio Okapi","publication_date":"2022-09-20","url":"https://www.radiookapi.net/2022/09/20/actualite/justice/rdc-ouverture-dune-information-judiciaire-lencontre-de-vidiye-tshimanga","claim":"The Kinshasa-Gombe prosecutor opened a judicial inquiry into Vidiye Tshimanga and asked the APLC to investigate allegations that he negotiated a 20 percent commission from supposed mining investors using his influence.","locator":"lines 151-156","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Local outlet reporting the procedural step taken by the prosecutor and anti-corruption agency; the underlying allegation remained unproven at publication.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Within 2022 and directly about a former presidential adviser in Tshisekedi's orbit.","ruler_attribution":"Indirect but material: the inquiry concerns an ex-presidential adviser and the use of influence attached to Tshisekedi's office.","contrary_evidence":["The underlying conduct was still an allegation at this stage, not a conviction."],"lenses":["7B.6","7B.7"]}
- Le Temps is useful because it confirms the scandal led to resignation and notes that later excerpts did not overturn the earlier incriminating statements.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Un haut responsable congolais demissionne a la suite des revelations du Temps","publisher":"Le Temps","publication_date":"2022-09-17","url":"https://www.letemps.ch/monde/afrique/un-haut-responsable-congolais-demissionne-suite-revelations-temps","claim":"Le Temps reported that Tshimanga resigned after the investigation and said the later audio excerpts he supplied did not invalidate his earlier statements about offshore structures or acting on the president's behalf.","locator":"opening paragraphs and closing paragraphs","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Independent Swiss investigative reporting on the same video evidence, with a clear note that later excerpts did not erase the earlier admissions.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Within 2022 and directly about the same resignation and taped meetings.","ruler_attribution":"Indirect through a cabinet-level aide who referenced the presidency and the president's campaign.","contrary_evidence":["Tshimanga said the material was a trap and that his remarks were taken out of context."],"lenses":["7B.3","7B.4","7B.5","7B.8","7B.10"]}
- OCCRP’s audit story is the strongest direct positive item on Tshisekedi’s own use of authority. It says he commissioned the IGF audit into Gecamines and that the report found severe irregularities and embezzlement.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"DR Congo State Mining Company Subject to a Damning Audit","publisher":"OCCRP","publication_date":"2022-06-16","url":"https://www.occrp.org/en/news/dr-congo-state-mining-company-subject-to-a-damning-audit","claim":"The IGF audit into Gecamines was commissioned by President Felix Tshisekedi and found severe irregularities, including embezzlement; the report said $414 million disappeared from claimed tax and loan payments.","locator":"lines 42-48","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Independent investigative reporting based on an audit report seen by OCCRP, with clear presidential attribution for commissioning the audit.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Within 2022, though the audit covered earlier years and was commissioned in 2021 before being reported in 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Direct: Tshisekedi ordered the audit and the report concerns a major state asset under his authority.","contrary_evidence":["The underlying losses predate 2022 and the article reports the audit rather than an independent courtroom finding."],"lenses":["7B.6","7B.7","7B.9","7B.10"]}
- Reuters gives the companion account: more than $400 million could not be traced, and Tshisekedi overhauled Gecamines leadership by replacing executives linked to previous corruption allegations.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Congo auditor says 400 million went missing from state mining company","publisher":"Reuters","publication_date":"2022-06-04","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/congo-auditor-says-400-million-went-missing-from-state-mining-company-2833518","claim":"Reuters reported that more than $400 million in Gecamines payments could not be found and that Tshisekedi overhauled Gecamines leadership, replacing executives most closely connected to previous corruption allegations.","locator":"lines 426-442","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters summarizes the watchdog audit and gives a concrete presidential response, but the underlying audit report itself was not publicly released in full.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Within 2022 and directly about a state asset and the president's response to it.","ruler_attribution":"Direct for the leadership overhaul; indirect for the missing funds because they concern a state company and prior management.","contrary_evidence":["The missing funds and alleged misappropriation are attributed to the company and prior managers, not to Tshisekedi personally."],"lenses":["7B.6","7B.7","7B.9","7B.10"]}
- ACP reports a president-led effort to recover state real estate improperly held by third parties and to tighten legal controls over public assets.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Le President Felix-Antoine Tshisekedi insiste sur la necessite de sauvegarder le patrimoine immobilier de l'Etat","publisher":"ACP","publication_date":"2022-09-16","url":"https://acp.cd/nation/le-president-felix-antoine-tshisekedi-insiste-sur-la-necessite-de-sauvegarder-le-patrimoine-immobilier-de-letat/","claim":"Tshisekedi encouraged the government to recover state real estate held or acquired unlawfully by third parties and to ensure transparency and respect for the law, while imposing stricter controls on any disposal of public assets.","locator":"lines 172-176","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"National news agency reporting a presidential council instruction; strong for the fact of the instruction, but still a government account rather than an outside audit.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly within 2022 and tied to a council meeting chaired by Tshisekedi.","ruler_attribution":"Direct: the instruction is attributed to Tshisekedi in a meeting he chaired.","contrary_evidence":["The article reports the instruction, not independently measured recovery or implementation."],"lenses":["7B.3","7B.6","7B.9","7B.10"]}
- The state-of-the-nation speech is self-report, but it is still relevant as a public accountability statement and shows what Tshisekedi chose to claim in late 2022.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Discours du President de la Republique Felix Tshisekedi sur l'etat de la nation","publisher":"Presidence RDC","publication_date":"2022-12-10","url":"https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/discours_du_president_de_la_republique_felix_tshisekedi_sur_letat_de_la_nation","claim":"The presidency said Tshisekedi's state-of-the-nation speech reviewed efforts on anti-corruption, universal health coverage, education, youth entrepreneurship, public revenue mobilization, elections, and public administration modernization.","locator":"lines 73-74","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Official speech text is reliable for what was said, but it is self-report rather than independent proof of implementation or honesty.","final_evidence_use":"context","period_fit":"Exactly within the 2022 target year.","ruler_attribution":"Direct self-presentation by Tshisekedi, but it is not independent verification.","contrary_evidence":["It is a promotional summary, not an external finding that the claims were true or fully implemented."],"lenses":["7B.2","7B.8","7B.10"]}
- The 2 September council minutes are a stronger concrete directive than the annual speech: Tshisekedi told magistrates to serve the nation, reaffirmed judicial independence, and ordered reforms to public-finance governance and payroll exclusions.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Compte rendu de la soixante-septieme reunion du Conseil des Ministres","publisher":"Presidence RDC","publication_date":"2022-09-02","url":"https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/compte_rendu_de_la_soixante_septieme_reunion_du_conseil_des_ministres","claim":"Tshisekedi told newly sworn magistrates to serve the nation and not themselves, reaffirmed respect for judicial independence, and ordered reforms of public-finance governance and payroll mechanization to reduce exclusion and disparities.","locator":"lines 85-102","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Official minutes provide a strong record of the instruction itself, but not independent proof that the reforms were implemented as described.","final_evidence_use":"context","period_fit":"Within 2022 and directly tied to a council meeting chaired by the president.","ruler_attribution":"Direct instruction by Tshisekedi in his capacity as head of state and chair of the council.","contrary_evidence":["The source records instructions rather than completed reforms or measurable outcomes."],"lenses":["7B.6","7B.7","7B.9","7B.10"]}
- The IMF report is an independent triangulation source: it says the program was based on Tshisekedi’s vision and also urged stronger governance tools such as beneficial-ownership disclosure, asset declarations, and independent anti-corruption institutions.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Democratic Republic of the Congo Staff Report for the 2022 Article IV Consultation, Second Review under the Extended Credit Facility Arrangement","publisher":"International Monetary Fund","publication_date":"2022-07-05","url":"https://www.elibrary.imf.org/view/journals/002/2022/210/article-A001-en.xml","claim":"The IMF report said the DRC program was based on Tshisekedi's vision and recommended stronger governance and transparency measures, including beneficial-ownership disclosure in procurement, an asset-declaration regime for politically exposed persons and close associates, and independent anti-corruption institutions.","locator":"Appendix I, Letter of Intent para. 1; governance recommendations table on business environment, governance and corruption","source_type":"IGO","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Independent IMF country report with explicit governance recommendations and a direct statement of the authorities' program frame.","final_evidence_use":"context","period_fit":"Within 2022 and directly about the Tshisekedi government’s program.","ruler_attribution":"Indirect: this is the external reform agenda for the Tshisekedi administration, not proof of Tshisekedi's personal honesty.","contrary_evidence":["Recommendations imply gaps in current practice; they do not prove clean personal conduct."],"lenses":["7B.6","7B.8","7B.9","7B.10"]}

**Search And Rejection**
- I considered roughly 30 documents across Reuters syndications, OCCRP, Le Temps, Radio Okapi, ACP, presidency.gov, the IMF, HRW, Freedom House, and several local/mining outlets.
- I kept 10 distinct URLs because they added materially different claims, not just paraphrases.
- I collapsed duplicate scandal coverage into a small chronology: initial sting report, Reuters resignation/office reaction, judicial inquiry, and a French-language recap.
- I rejected later 2023-2026 items, including fact-checks, election-procurement stories, and other post-period material.
- I rejected 2021-only or 2021-framed items when they did not describe a 2022 act by Tshisekedi.
- I rejected generic country-level corruption and press-freedom material when it did not establish a direct personal nexus.
- I rejected most political-freedom and social/economic chapter evidence unless it clearly connected to Tshisekedi personally or to his close governing network.
- I also rejected repetitive syndications that only repeated the same allegation without adding a new step in the chronology or a new attribution point.

**Remaining Gaps**
- I still do not have direct primary evidence on Tshisekedi’s own assets, family businesses, gifts, or outside interests in 2022.
- I still do not have hard evidence on his own campaign finance, beneficial ownership, or private enrichment.
- The strongest negative evidence is still mostly about a close adviser and the wider governing circle, not about Tshisekedi personally taking money.
- I did not find a strong independent finding that Tshisekedi himself knowingly lied to the public on a specific 2022 integrity issue.
- More searching would help on asset-declaration filings, procurement records, campaign financing, and any investigative work on presidential-family or presidential-office holdings.
